course_description:
Software testing is critical for ensuring the delivery of high-quality software systems. This course introduces foundational principles, techniques, and practices that support effective software testing, with a focus on evaluating and testing both human-written and AI- generated code. As AI-assisted programming becomes more prevalent, it is essential to adapt and enhance traditional testing techniques to effectively validate AI-generated software artifacts. Students will develop practical skills in designing, implementing, and assessing software testing strategies. The course also considers how these practices fit within agile and DevOps workflows, preparing students to meet the evolving needs of modern software development.

AI tools may be used to support learning and task completion in this course, and the course provides guidance on appropriate use. Students are expected to apply judgement when using these tools, to check outputs carefully, and to ensure that all submitted work reflects their own understanding. Students are responsible for ensuring that any use of AI complies with academic integrity requirements and is appropriately acknowledged.

course_aims: This course teaches the principles and practical techniques of software testing and automation. It equips students with the skills to systematically detect software faults, design effective test cases, and apply automated testing tools in modern software development practices.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain the fundamental principles and objectives of software testing.
Identify and describe different types of software testing techniques.
Design and implement effective test cases and test plans.
Use software testing tools and Generative AI techniques to support test automation.
Perform static and dynamic analysis of software artifacts.
Evaluate software quality using metrics and coverage criteria.

assessment_details.title: Assignment One
assessment_details.task_description: This assignment will provide practice at solving a set of testing problems. You may also be asked to attend an interview about your submission (see the Additional assessment information section below). This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools.
